TYPES.name: 3D letters
TYPES.label: 3D letters
TYPES.meta: Built-up 3D letter signs made in Gateshead: fabricated face-lit and halo-lit letters, Komacel letters with brass or mirror inlays, and acrylic letters. Fixed to the wall or on a panel.
TYPES.desc: Letters with real depth that stand proud of the wall. We make three kinds: fabricated metal letters (aluminium, stainless, copper or brass), Komacel letters and acrylic letters, fixed straight to the wall on stand-off locators or mounted on a panel.
spec: Fabricated (aluminium, stainless, copper or brass), Komacel, acrylic
Copper and brass, including aged finishes
Halo-lit only; inset-routed for brass, copper, Trotec metallics or mirrored acrylic
Translucent, so light passes through the letter
Straight to the wall on stand-off locators, or on a panel

variants.p: Built from a metal face and folded returns in aluminium, stainless steel, copper or brass, including aged finishes. The most versatile option, and the one to choose for large or high-level letters.

Cut from solid Komacel, then inset-routed so the face can be filled with brass, copper or Trotec metallic laminates, a cheaper route to a brushed-metal finish. Mirrored acrylic in gold, silver or rose gold works too.
Solid acrylic lets light pass through, so letters glow when lit from behind. Often mounted on a panel, like our glow. fascia.

notes: Every letter can go straight onto the wall on stand-off locators, or onto a panel when the wall isn't suitable or you want a backdrop.
The Vault: fabricated, halo-lit letters on a panel. Jet2: halo-lit fabricated letters straight onto the wall. Dog & Parrot: inset brass Komacel.
Fabricated letters also come in copper and brass, including aged finishes.
Not sure which suits your budget? We'll mock up the options on a photo of your building.
faq: What's the difference between face-lit and halo-lit?

Face-lit letters glow through the front face, with light contained by the rim and returns. Halo-lit letters have a solid face and throw light back onto the wall behind, creating a glow around each letter.
Can Komacel letters be face-lit?
No. Komacel letters are halo-lit only. If you want the face itself to glow, fabricated or acrylic letters are the better choice.
Can letters go straight onto brick or cladding?
Yes. We fix them on stand-off locators so they sit off the wall. If the surface isn't suitable, we mount them on a panel instead.

TYPES.name: Backlit panels
TYPES.label: backlit panels
TYPES.seo_title: Backlit Panel Signs: Illuminated Aperture-Cut Panels
TYPES.meta: Illuminated backlit panel signs designed and fabricated in Gateshead. Shaped or rectangular panels with cut-through graphics that glow at night.
TYPES.desc: One of our most popular signs. A fabricated panel with your name and logo aperture-cut through it and filled with push-through opal acrylic, lit from inside with LEDs so the graphics glow at night and read crisply by day. Bar Seventy Three and Cod & Crust are good examples.
spec: Fabricated aluminium, powder-coated to any colour
Aperture-cut through the face, with push-through opal acrylic
Internal LEDs, so only the graphics glow
Rectangular or cut to the outline of your logo
notes: Panels can be shaped around your logo, as with Bar Seventy Three, or kept as a clean rectangle.
Everything is cut, folded and wired in our own workshop.
faq: Does the whole panel light up?
No. Only the cut-through graphics glow; the rest of the panel stays solid, which is what gives backlit panels their crisp look at night.
Can the panel be a custom shape?
Yes. Panels can follow the outline of your logo or be a simple rectangle.
Do you fit them too?
Yes. Our own fitting teams install every panel we make.

TYPES.name: Flat-cut letters
TYPES.label: flat-cut letters
TYPES.seo_title: Flat-Cut Letter Signs: CNC & Laser Cut Lettering
TYPES.meta: Flat-cut letters cut from solid sheet on our CNC and laser in Gateshead. Crisp, cost-effective lettering for receptions, offices and exteriors.
TYPES.desc: Letters cut from solid sheet on our CNC router and laser, with a crisp flat face and no returns. A clean, cost-effective way to put a name on a wall, inside or out.
spec: Acrylic, foamex, aluminium composite, stainless steel
notes: Flat-cut letters cost less than 3D letters and suit interiors especially well.
Pantera Advisory Group is cut from foamex, a light, rigid PVC board.
faq: Are flat-cut letters illuminated?
Usually not. If you want lighting, 3D letters or a backlit panel are the better route.
Can they be used outside?
Yes, in exterior-grade materials such as aluminium composite or stainless steel.

spec: Fabricated letters, letters on panels, printed Dibond, vinyl on fabricated panels
Powered access by our IPAF and PASMA trained teams
Engineered for cladding, brick and curtain wall
notes: Rolls-Royce: large high-level letters on cladding.

faq: Do you handle high-level installs?
Yes. Our IPAF and PASMA trained crews install from powered access, including on live hospital and campus sites.
Will my building sign need planning permission?
Many illuminated or large signs need advertisement consent. We'll tell you at the survey stage and can prepare the drawings you need.

TYPES.meta: Double-sided projecting signs made in Gateshead, so you're seen from along the street. Round, square or bespoke, lit or non-lit.

Fabricated tray with acrylic or printed faces

TYPES.name: Light boxes
TYPES.label: light boxes
TYPES.seo_title: Light Box Signs | Illuminated Shop Signs
TYPES.meta: Illuminated light box signs made in our Gateshead factory: aluminium boxes with acrylic faces lit evenly from inside, for shopfronts and projecting signs.
TYPES.desc: A light box is an aluminium box with an acrylic face, lit evenly from inside by LEDs. Light boxes are generally smaller signs, ideal for shopfronts, projecting signs and anywhere the whole face should glow.
spec: Fabricated aluminium box, painted to any colour
LED modules, lit evenly across the face
Rectangular, round or cut to your logo
notes: Light boxes suit smaller, crisp signs. Once a sign gets large, a flex face avoids joins in the face.
faq: How big can a light box be?
Acrylic faces come in sheets, so light boxes suit smaller signs. For large fascias we'd recommend a flex face, which covers big areas without joins.
Can a light box be double-sided?
Yes. Double-sided light boxes work well as projecting signs, lit on both faces.

TYPES.name: Flex faces
TYPES.label: flex faces
TYPES.seo_title: Flex Face Signs | Large Illuminated Signs
TYPES.meta: Large-scale flex face signs made in Gateshead: a printed flex fabric skin tensioned across an illuminated frame, seamless at any size and re-skinnable for a rebrand.
TYPES.desc: A flex face is built for scale. A printed flex fabric skin is tensioned across a large illuminated frame, so even very big signs go up in one seamless face. When you rebrand, the skin can be replaced without changing the frame.
spec: Printed flex fabric, tensioned in the frame
LED, lit evenly across the face
Large-scale, with no joins in the face
notes: Kosmic Kingdom is a large flex face: one seamless printed skin across the whole frame.
faq: When should I choose a flex face over a light box?
Once a sign gets large, acrylic faces need joins. A flex face covers big areas in one seamless skin.
Can you replace just the face?
Yes. That's the big advantage of a flex face: a new printed skin goes into the existing frame for a rebrand.

TYPES.desc: The glow of classic neon made with modern LED flex: low voltage, cool to the touch and far tougher than glass. Ideal for statement walls, bars and photo moments.
spec: Clear, coloured or mirrored acrylic, cut to shape
Warm white, ice white and a full colour range
Low-voltage, plug-in or hard-wired, dimmable options
notes: Send us your logo or a line of text and we'll draw it up in neon.
faq: Is LED neon safe indoors?
Yes. It runs at low voltage and stays cool to the touch, unlike glass neon.
Can it go outside?
Yes, using outdoor-rated LED neon and fittings.
